title: Reconstruct the extraction incident
description: Select an incident, the evidence envelope that survived, and a recovery action. The ledger reveals whether the accepted result can be explained and repaired without erasing history.

bundles.label: Normalized output only
bundles.detail: The store kept the final JSON but discarded source anchors, versions, validator results, and attempt history.

bundles.label: Anchored and versioned candidate
bundles.detail: Each field retains source evidence, processor and schema identity, validation outcomes, and accepted history.

bundles.label: Complete replay ledger
bundles.detail: The anchored candidate also preserves review corrections and every idempotent processing attempt.

actions.label: Retry and overwrite
actions.detail: Run the current default processor and replace the accepted JSON in place.
actions.restores: Nothing reproducible; the old evidence and decision disappear.

actions.label: Replay into a candidate and diff
actions.detail: Pin the source and versions, create a new candidate, compare fields and gates, then promote explicitly.
actions.restores: A reproducible before-and-after decision with rollback.

actions.label: Re-review from source anchors
actions.detail: Open the affected regions, record bounded corrections, and create a reviewed revision.
actions.restores: Human confirmation tied to the exact source evidence.

actions.label: Quarantine and re-establish source identity
actions.detail: Stop processing until the original bytes, page set, and source ownership are reconciled.
actions.restores: A trustworthy input boundary before any new candidate is accepted.

actions.label: Reconcile accepted state before retry
actions.detail: Check the accepted store and attempt ledger to determine whether the timed-out promotion committed.
actions.restores: One accepted version for one processing intent.

incidents.label: Parser upgrade changes invoice total
incidents.detail: A canary candidate changes the total after a processor-version upgrade, while the source file is unchanged.
incidents.safeConsequence: Replay both pinned versions, inspect the anchored total, compare validator outcomes, and promote only a passing candidate.
incidents.wrongConsequence: Overwriting makes the regression look like the historical truth and removes a rapid rollback target.
incidents.recoveryTarget: Explain the value change without mutating accepted-v12.

incidents.label: The source object changed under the same URI
incidents.detail: A replay reads a different byte hash from the object key stored on the original job.
incidents.safeConsequence: Quarantine the mutable object, recover the original immutable bytes, and assign a new revision if the replacement is legitimate.
incidents.wrongConsequence: Comparing parser output from different inputs misdiagnoses a source-integrity incident as a model change.
incidents.recoveryTarget: Restore a one-to-one link between document revision and byte hash.

incidents.label: A customer disputes a reviewed field
incidents.detail: A human correction changed the effective date, but the reason and source region are needed to resolve the dispute.
incidents.symptom: Reviewed value lacks a defensible trail
incidents.safeConsequence: Open the exact page region, inspect the reviewer correction and reason, then record any new correction as another revision.
incidents.wrongConsequence: A fresh model run cannot explain why a person changed the field or whether the correction was justified.
incidents.recoveryTarget: Resolve the dispute while preserving both model and reviewer history.

incidents.label: Promotion timed out after the write
incidents.detail: The worker did not observe the response that confirms whether candidate-v22 became accepted.
incidents.safeConsequence: Read accepted state with the processing intent ID. Retry the compare-and-swap only if candidate-v22 is not already committed.
incidents.wrongConsequence: Treating the timeout as failure can duplicate a promotion event or overwrite a later accepted revision.
incidents.recoveryTarget: Determine authoritative completion before issuing another write.
